subject: RE: HealthEdge RFI — KEK wrapping, TLS SNI, and BYO key clarifications
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@healthedge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Cohen <leah.cohen@healthedge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HealthEdge RFI: KEK wrapping, TLS SNI and BYO clarifications

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the initial RFI deliverable. A couple of clarifications from our security team on the key-management side before we proceed to the legal questionnaire:

1) KEK wrapping: Do you support customer-supplied key-encryption-keys (BYO KEK) that are used to wrap tenant DEKs before they are stored in your KMS? If yes, please state the supported wrap algorithms and whether wrap/unwrap happens inside a FIPS-140 validated HSM.

2) HSM attestation: We need an attestation showing the HSM model/version, FIPS level, and a recent signed snapshot of key policy bindings (or a link to a downloadable artifact).

3) TLS SNI and multi-tenant endpoints: We operate multiple subsidiaries and will use SNI to route TLS traffic. Does SNI routing affect your certificate validation or client IP-based routing? Are TLS certs terminated at the same layer across tenants?

4) Key rotation and emergency rotation: What guarantees do you provide for forced rotation (e.g., compromise event) — do you support rewrap-with-new-KEK for historical data? What's the retention of previous KEKs and can HealthEdge request zeroization?

If you can point us to an attestation doc and a short diagram of the TLS layers, we can share these with compliance. Ideally within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Marco
Senior InfoSec Manager
HealthEdge

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: HealthEdge RFI: KEK wrapping, TLS SNI and BYO clarifications

Marco —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers first, with attachments and a technical follow-up from Rishi below.

1) BYO KEK / KEK wrapping: Yes — Redwood supports customer-supplied KEKs (BYO-KEK) used to wrap tenant DEKs. We perform wrap/unwrap operations inside an HSM-backed key-wrapping service. Supported wrapping algorithms: RSA-OAEP-256 for asymmetric wrap (HSM wrap key), and AES-KW (RFC 3394) for symmetric KEK wrapping. We include envelope encryption where the DEK is encrypted with a data-key (DEK) and the DEK is wrapped by the customer-supplied KEK.

2) HSM attestation: Attached is our KEK wrapping process PDF and a KEK attestation template. Rishi will attach the signed attestation snapshot and HSM details (model, firmware, FIPS level).

3) TLS SNI / multi-tenant endpoints: We terminate TLS at the edge LB which is SNI-aware. Certificate validation and client TLS handshake behave the same regardless of SNI; SNI is used purely for virtual host selection. We do not perform client-IP-based routing at TLS termination — that happens post-termination in our routing layer. See attached tls-sni-multi-tenant-diagram.png for the layer breakdown.

4) Rotation / emergency rewrap: We support forced rewrap flows where historical DEKs can be rewrapped under a new KEK without decrypting the underlying ciphertext (re-enveloping). We maintain a KEK lifecycle policy and can perform zeroization upon written request, subject to contract/regulatory retention clauses. More specifics below.

Attachments: redwood-kek-wrapping-process.pdf, tls-sni-multi-tenant-diagram.png, kek-attestation-template.docx

Next steps: Rishi will provide the HSM attestation artifact and the policy excerpt for emergency rewrap. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call if your team wants a diagram walkthrough.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: HealthEdge RFI: KEK wrapping, TLS SNI and BYO clarifications

Marco —

Following up with the technical artifacts and specifics you requested. Summary first, then artifacts/links:

- HSM platform: We use SafeHSM Model X4-2026 (firmware 4.2.1), deployed in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated modules in our primary and DR regions. The attestation snapshot includes module serials and firmware checksums.

- Wrapping algorithms and flow: Symmetric KEK wrapping uses AES-KW (RFC 3394) with 256-bit KEKs. Asymmetric wrap (customer requests) supported via RSA-OAEP-256 where customers provide an RSA public key that we store as a wrapping target inside the HSM. Wrap/unwrap logic executes entirely within the HSM boundary; plaintext DEKs are never exposed outside the HSM memory.

- KEK retention & zeroization: We retain KEK wrap-key metadata (keyID, wrapping-algorithm, creation_ts) for audit purposes. The wrapped key material may exist in storage until zeroized; upon a formal zeroization request we zeroize the KEK material from all active vaults and provide a signed confirmation. Note: zeroization of customer KEKs is subject to any agreed data-retention terms and cannot retroactively decrypt data already re-enveloped under a different KEK without the original KEK.

- Emergency rotation / rewrap: We support re-enveloping historical DEKs by performing a wrap-with-new-KEK operation inside the HSM. This operation does not decrypt the data payloads at the application layer; it rewraps the DEK envelope. We provide a job-based rewrap process, with audit logs and an estimated throughput (keys/sec) for planning.

Artifacts (links):
1) HSM attestation snapshot (signed): https://evidence.redwood.com/attestations/kek-2027-12-docsig
2) KEK wrap job runbook and throughput guide: https://drive.redwood.com/controls/HE-KEK-WRAP-2027
3) Crypto policy excerpt: https://drive.redwood.com/controls/crypto-policy-2027

Operational notes:
- SNI: Because TLS termination happens at our edge and is SNI-aware, each tenant can use a distinct certificate; certificate management can be self-served or delegated to Redwood. We do not surface tenant certificate private key material to customers when we manage certs — for BYO-cert scenarios, you can provide a certificate chain and private key through our secure onboarding workflow (or use a delegated ACME integration).

- Auditability: All wrap/unwrap and rewrap jobs emit tokens in our event store and are tied to requestor identity and job-id for audit. We store these logs per your retention request (configurable).

If helpful I can attach the signed attestation PDF to this thread — I've uploaded the doc and included the DocuSign link above.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied Crypto Engineer
Redwood Inference

- We will need a signed attestation (DocuSign) using the kek-attestation-template.docx from your attachments. Can you route that to me (Marco.ruiz@healthedge.com) and cc Leah?

- For emergency rewrap: compliance wants the estimated max rewrap throughput and an example job-id/audit record for an internal test run. Are you able to run a small test rewrap on a non-prod tenant and share the audit token?

If you can provide the signed attestation and the rewrap test audit token by Monday EOD, we'll move this into the contract queue.

Appreciate it — Marco
